name: cayley
desc: Graph database inspired by Freebase and Knowledge Graph
why: A graph database with a Freebase lineage and a query language twist, an unusual corner of databases.

brief.what_it_is: Cayley is an open-source graph database for Linked Data, modeled on the graph store behind Google's Knowledge Graph (formerly Freebase). It stores graph data, including RDF formats such as NQuads and JSON-LD, and sits on top of an existing backend store (the homepage lists SQL, NoSQL or key-value). You query it through one of three languages: Gizmo, a Gremlin-inspired language; a GraphQL-inspired language; or MQL, a simplified Freebase-style query language. The README also lists a built-in query editor, visualizer and REPL.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as an open-source take on the graph database behind Google's Knowledge Graph, aimed at people working with Linked Data. The homepage stresses that it is built for linked data and is meant to be extensible rather than locked to one data model.
brief.how_it_works: Cayley is modular: the homepage says new formats, backends, query languages or custom logic can be added. The README says it is optimized for use inside applications and gives a performance example: 134 million quads in LevelDB on 2014 consumer hardware, with a multi-hop intersection query (films starring X and Y) taking about 150ms. Beyond that, the fetched pages do not explain the storage or query internals.
brief.install_notes: The fetched pages show no install commands, so I could not confirm anything beyond the brew formula's executable named cayley. The README links a Snap Store listing (snapcraft.io/cayley). The docs index has pages for Install Cayley, Configuration, Running in Docker, Running in Kubernetes, and Quick Start as a Go library, but I did not open them, so I cannot say what first-run setup involves.
brief.standout: Few graph databases give you Freebase's MQL alongside a Gremlin-style language and a GraphQL-style language over the same data. It is also built to sit on top of a database you already run, rather than replacing it.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage copyright line reads 2021. The docs index page says 'Last updated 4 years ago' with no date shown. The README links a GitHub Actions build badge, but I saw no release date or latest commit date, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The README's performance figures come from 2014 consumer hardware and are rough by its own description. The docs index I fetched is only a table of contents, so my picture of setup and usage is thin. Licensing is Apache 2.0 according to the homepage. The Slack invite link points to a herokuapp.com host that may be stale.
quotes: Open-source graph inspired by the graph database behind Freebase and Google's Knowledge Graph.
Support multiple query languages: Gizmo (Gremlin dialect), MQL and GraphQL dialect.
Production ready: well tested and used by various companies for their production workloads
